subject: literature
passage: Tomasz had promised to be the first seller in the square, so he was up long before dawn, checking the cart against the list his grandmother had dictated. Everything was there: three sacks of rye, ground the night before; a crate of eggs, each wrapped in ______ and the jar of plum preserves that she had insisted, over all his objections, would fetch the best price at the market in town.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The colon introduces a list of three items, and each item contains its own comma: "three sacks of rye, ground the night before" and "a crate of eggs, each wrapped in straw." When list items contain commas, semicolons separate the items. A semicolon already follows the first item, so one must follow the second as well.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Because the items contain commas, a comma here would not clearly mark where the second item ends; the items must be separated by semicolons, as the first two are.
explanation.B: Incorrect. With no punctuation, the second and third items run together, and the eggs seem to be wrapped in straw "and the jar of plum preserves."
explanation.C: Incorrect. A colon can't separate items in a list, and the sentence already uses a colon to introduce the list.
explanation.D: Correct. The semicolon separates the second item from the third, matching the semicolon after the first item.
